_why: dream_lint.py rewrites files in a shared, unversioned memory store. These rows prove the tests notice if a guard that keeps the rewrite safe stops working: links inside code, the unique-target rule, the changed-since-read skip, the backup, and the exit code for an unreadable store.
_provenance: memory-dream/SKILL.md; Anthropic 'components of agent memory' dreaming cookbook (2026-11).

mutations.name: ambiguous-treated-as-fixable
mutations._mechanism: Any normalised hit counts as a unique target, so a link matching two files is rewritten to an arbitrary one.

mutations.name: no-backup
mutations._mechanism: The file is rewritten without a backup copy; the store is not under version control.

mutations.name: unreadable-exits-zero
mutations._mechanism: A store with no MEMORY.md is reported with exit 0, indistinguishable from a clean store.

mutations.name: fence-length-ignored
mutations._mechanism: A shorter closing fence ends a longer one, so a code example's links are rewritten.

mutations.name: fenced-code-scanned
mutations._mechanism: The fence's opening line is left unmasked, so a link in its info string is read.

mutations.name: indented-scanned
mutations._mechanism: Indented code lines are read as prose.

mutations.name: no-roundtrip
mutations._mechanism: The replacement spelling is not required to resolve back to the same file.

mutations.name: nonlink-replacement
mutations._mechanism: A quoted or dotted slug is used as the replacement, turning a link into a non-link.
mutations.find: if (cand and not NONLINK.search(cand) and not

mutations.name: name-from-body
mutations._mechanism: name: is read anywhere in the file, so body text supplies the slug.
mutations.find:
fm = FRONTMATTER.match(text)
    if not fm:
        return None
    m = NAME.search(fm.group(1))

mutations.name: hash-from-second-read
mutations._mechanism: Hashes are re-taken at apply time instead of from the read the fix was built from, so an edit in between is clobbered.
mutations.find:
for name in store.topics:
        new = fixed_text(store, name)

mutations.name: changed-file-not-skipped
mutations._mechanism: The final re-hash is ignored, so a concurrent session's write is clobbered.

mutations.name: crlf-translated
mutations._mechanism: Text is decoded with newline translation, so CRLF files become LF.

mutations.name: mode-lost
mutations._mechanism: The temp file's 0600 mode replaces the original's.

mutations.name: dangling-rewritten
mutations._mechanism: A link with no target is classified FIXABLE instead of DANGLING.

mutations.name: apply-oserror-uncaught
mutations._mechanism: An I/O error during --apply escapes as a traceback (exit 1) instead of exit 2.
mutations.find:
except OSError as exc:
                print(f"DREAM_LINT: IO_ERROR
mutations.replace:
except ValueError as exc:
                print(f"DREAM_LINT: IO_ERROR

mutations.name: non-utf8-exit-1
mutations._mechanism: A decode error is not caught as unreadable.
mutations.find:
except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError) as exc:
        print(f"DREAM_LINT: UNREADABLE

mutations.name: code-span-unmasked
mutations._mechanism: Code spans are not masked, so a backticked [[link]] is rewritten.

mutations.name: span-crosses-blank-line
mutations._mechanism: A lone backtick masks everything up to the next backtick, paragraphs away.
mutations.find: limit = next((b for b in blanks if b >= opener.end()), len(text))

mutations.name: span-closes-on-any-run
mutations._mechanism: Any backtick run closes a span, so a longer inner run ends it and exposes a link in code.

mutations.name: bracket-or-pipe-slug-written
mutations._mechanism: A slug containing ]] or | is accepted, writing [[x]]y]] or [[pipe|name]], links that point elsewhere.

mutations.name: symlink-replaced
mutations._mechanism: A symlinked topic is replaced by a regular file, leaving the real target stale.

mutations.name: hardlink-split
mutations._mechanism: A hard-linked topic is replaced, splitting it from its twin.

mutations.name: archived-counted-as-live
mutations._mechanism: Archive-only notes are reported as split candidates, so already-archived records are proposed for archiving or splitting.
